GOFATHOM — PROJECT APPROACH 1.1
Canonical human/AI blueprint. All decisions are proposals unless explicitly marked otherwise.

METADATA:
  title: GoFathom — Project Approach 1.1
  version: 1.1
  date: 2026-10-18
  status: Debated foundation • proposed design • implementation not audited
  lineage: GoFathom is the new name for SupaBiz. Historical SupaBiz editions remain unchanged.
  purpose: Help a business see what is pending, who owns it, and the evidence behind it; then safely coordinate and verify the next action.
  evidence: 18 bounded project reviews, earlier harness research, and two rounds of Claude critique. Eleven reviews include selected source/client/examples; seven are public-product reviews. No complete vendor security audit, customer validation or new product benchmark is claimed.
  limits: 298 learning entries are candidate observations, not 298 independent validations; they previously used 20 rationale templates. No measured uplift, customer willingness to pay or production readiness is established.
  schema version: 1.1.0
  prior version: ../gofathom/
  reviewed commit: 09bd2acd9fc1600866c7816e7daa565e85c0ebd3
  revision method: All twelve decisions were critiqued in Claude’s gofathom chat, rebutted by Codex and adjudicated. Agreement is not implementation evidence or customer validation.
DEBATE SUMMARY:
  status: Three completed critique/rebuttal rounds; no remaining blocking objection from Claude, with explicit Codex qualifications adopted.
  reviewer scope: Claude read canonical JSON core sections at commit 09bd2ac, critique.txt and the repaired synthesis. It inspected the 18 project entries and 76 packages structurally, sampled stage examples/comparisons, and did not re-read all project reports, HTML, diagrams, ZIP or text/JSON parity. This is a document review, not a code audit.
  ROUNDS:
    [1]
      round: 1
      purpose: All twelve decisions challenged against stages/contracts/roadmap/cost.

    [2]
      round: 2
      purpose: Codex rebutted invariants, cancellation, source scope, risk and measurement claims; Claude revised recommendations.

    [3]
      round: 3
      purpose: Final qualifications on processing gaps, conservative transmit markers, harmful restrictive instructions, risk assurance and attested values; Claude accepted them.
  QUALIFIED OR REJECTED:
    [1]
      One event → one candidate: replaced with revision accounting and many-to-many evidence.

    [2]
      After claim means too late: replaced with fenced before-send marker, conservative unknown outcomes and verified cancellation.

    [3]
      Restrictive instructions are safe: rejected; delay, urgency and consequence remain part of risk.

    [4]
      Canaries alone establish rare-event recall: rejected; known-path tests and natural observations are reported separately.

    [5]
      Natural data alone is mandatory/sufficient for reliance: replaced with an authorized, risk-specific assurance case.

    [6]
      Rank or specificity silently overrides a hold: rejected; explicit override capability/target required.

    [7]
      Opening evidence proves review quality: rejected; use outcome-oriented review exercises and spot checks.

    [8]
      Every linked session has identical scope, or Gmail label selection is provider-enforced: unverified assumptions; inspect each adapter.

    [9]
      No electronic API means no usable evidence: qualified; dated authorized scans/counts/attestations can support limited checks.

    [10]
      A paid commitment must precede discovery: rejected; keep bounded discovery separate from demand and reliance gates.
  next evidence: Actual code audit, permitted source access and real workflow observation. Another AI review cannot substitute for these.
  version applied: Foundation 1.1 incorporates the Codex qualifications and final mechanism additions. Foundation 1.0 stays unchanged.
ADJUDICATION:
  [1]
    id: GF-D01
    delivery gate: Pilot / G1
    disposition: Amend
    claude objection: Router-declined messages can disappear from every board lane.
    codex response: Accept complete intake accounting; reject one message → one candidate and terminal-only counts.
    accepted change: Account for each source revision and workflow evaluation as pending, excluded with reason, quarantined, failed or assessed. Assessed events link to zero or more candidates; candidate matching and work status remain separate. Audit exclusions and replay changed rules.
    acceptance or revisit test: Reconcile a fixed journal window including pending/failed items. One message creates several candidates; several messages support one candidate; an excluded critical item is found by independent review.

  [2]
    id: GF-D02
    delivery gate: Pilot / G1–G2
    disposition: Amend
    claude objection: The authority system is named in prose, but external edits can invalidate pending decisions.
    codex response: Accept C17; observation is bounded by actual connector capability, not a promised universal one-sync guarantee.
    accepted change: Bind each authoritative field to a system, source identity/version or hash, read method, observation window, write mode and cutover. Revalidate the bound revision before admission/writeback; external changes stale dependent checks.
    acceptance or revisit test: Edit a source while review is pending; require re-review. After cutover, conflicting edits to the former authority raise a dual-write exception.

  [3]
    id: GF-D03
    delivery gate: Before processing untrusted assets
    disposition: Retain with precise boundaries
    claude objection: An isolated parser may still hold broad database credentials and unrestricted egress.
    codex response: Accept worker profiles; differentiate untrusted parsers from trusted ingestion/effect services. Ordinary environment access is not itself a security failure.
    accepted change: Untrusted parser gets only the scoped asset, no production secrets or direct database access, restricted filesystem/egress, resource limits and a validated derivative-output API. Trusted workers receive separate least-privilege profiles.
    acceptance or revisit test: Deny forbidden socket/filesystem/credential access; bound resource exhaustion; allow legitimate derivative submission and inspect quarantined failures.

  [4]
    id: GF-D04
    delivery gate: Discovery / G0
    disposition: Amend
    claude objection: A module name can be mistaken for tested implementation; evidence labels are templated.
    codex response: Accept commit-pinned audit rows and divergent entrypoints. Historical par/CC-224 cases are reproduction targets, not asserted fail/pass results.
    accepted change: Audit every H/C responsibility with commit, code path or explicit absence, entrypoints, known divergent paths and test artifacts. Distinguish not audited, absent, partial, present-untested and tested-at-commit.
    acceptance or revisit test: Locate code and permitted fixtures; reproduce historical failures if available. A tested status requires pinned test evidence; the documentation template remains unfilled until then.

  [5]
    id: GF-D05
    delivery gate: Pilot / G1; review before runner expansion
    disposition: Amend
    claude objection: A simple runner can grow into an unowned workflow engine.
    codex response: Accept a charter and owner; reject an arbitrary one-timer cap, quarterly-only review and automatic Temporal adoption.
    accepted change: Register job states, timer types and transitions. Support leases/fences, classified retries, outbox and scoped cancellation. Complex signal graphs, child orchestration or in-flight definition migration trigger a comparative engine spike. Domain effect reconciliation remains required.
    acceptance or revisit test: Test crash, stale lease, timer, cancellation and upgrade recovery. Review complexity at phase exit and on new primitives or incidents; compare engineering and operating effort.

  [6]
    id: GF-D06
    delivery gate: Before any live source enrollment
    disposition: Amend
    claude objection: Selected groups may be a filter rather than a restriction at the provider.
    codex response: Accept source-enforced versus application-filtered distinctions; inspect the actual adapter instead of assuming all sessions or Gmail labels have identical scopes.
    accepted change: Disclose provider-visible scope and selected processing scope separately. Minimize nonselected content before durable capture, including controllable SDK cache/log/crash paths. Assess dedicated number/host, account risk and explicit exposure limits; reject incompatible deployments.
    acceptance or revisit test: Inject nonselected content in a controlled test and inspect journal, media, traces, cache and crash artifacts. State measured exclusions and unavoidable session exposure; do not promise zero traces without evidence.

  [7]
    id: GF-D07
    delivery gate: Pilot / chosen connectors
    disposition: Retain with operational risk checks
    claude objection: License checks miss protocol changes, provider terms and account restrictions.
    codex response: Accept an owner and fallback for external-service risks. Import success does not prove continuous capture.
    accepted change: Dependency records name provenance, rights, capabilities, provider/account constraints, failure owner and fallback mode with actual freshness limits. Only adopt what the chosen workflow needs.
    acceptance or revisit test: Exercise selected connector recovery and a permitted import fallback; label manual/delayed operation and gaps rather than presenting it as live continuity.

  [8]
    id: GF-D08
    delivery gate: Before first external action / G3
    disposition: Amend
    claude objection: Revocation, cancellation and a kill switch are underspecified once a request is in flight.
    codex response: Accept C06 policy/grant/epoch and cancellation evidence. Reject after claim = too late and atomic revocation across external systems.
    accepted change: Serialize local claims and durable before-send transmit markers with current grant/cancel epochs. A scope stop fences later boundaries. The marker means possible transmission, not success; earlier attempts may need reconciliation. Before-send prevention requires marker/fencing invariants on every path. Compensation is a new authorized action.
    acceptance or revisit test: Inject revocation/cancel before claim, between claim/send, during send, after remote commit and after lost response. UI only claims prevented/cancelled/completed when evidence warrants it; otherwise unknown.

  [9]
    id: GF-D09
    delivery gate: Workflow selection / G0
    disposition: Amend
    claude objection: A blanket text-first launch could exclude evidence needed by the chosen photo/voice workflow.
    codex response: Accept required modalities per workflow; native-text-first is an extraction preference, not a product restriction. Video remains conditional on need.
    accepted change: C16 records required input modalities, language/noise conditions and citation locator types. Use native structure when suitable; process required images/voice from the first selected slice.
    acceptance or revisit test: Score real permitted media by risk slice, wrong extraction and abstention. Show page/region/time locators where applicable and unsupported coverage explicitly.

  [10]
    id: GF-D10
    delivery gate: Pilot / G2; controls before rule activation
    disposition: Amend
    claude objection: Instruction conflict, override, expiry and change-class authority are not explicit.
    codex response: Accept semantic fields; reject rank-plus-specificity as a universal override rule and shadow activation as sufficient proof for every high-risk change.
    accepted change: Use policy-defined override capabilities, explicit target/supersedes links and scope checks. Hold incompatible unresolved rules. Define timezone/boundary/condition/release authority. Confirmation policy depends on target/risk; ambiguous or consequential changes require exact review.
    acceptance or revisit test: Cover owner hold versus subordinate release, ambiguous Friday, count-time thresholds, incompatible overlaps and action-in-flight supersession. Use replay/shadow plus protected future-case tests when risk requires.

  [11]
    id: GF-D11
    delivery gate: Pilot / G1 and every reliance expansion
    disposition: Amend
    claude objection: Intake cannot be the sole source of its own eligible-event denominator.
    codex response: Accept independent inventories with provenance and known shared failure modes. Reject canaries as the only way to estimate rare-event recall or proof of natural-event recall.
    accepted change: C10 separates source observation basis, known gaps and processing coverage. C16 identifies independent inventory/eligibility adjudication and denominator status. Report labeled real-event results, synthetic/canary results and unknown unseen coverage separately. Record risk-slice reliance in C18; combine appropriately limited evidence in an authorized assurance case rather than requiring or trusting one evidence type universally.
    acceptance or revisit test: Drop an event before intake and before routing; the comparison must detect or declare the unobservable gap. Live canaries require explicit consent and isolation from consequential workflows.

  [12]
    id: GF-D12
    delivery gate: Human roles when needed; automated delegation later
    disposition: Retain with clarification
    claude objection: A CA or authorized operator may serve several businesses before agent exchange exists.
    codex response: Accept scoped human roles now; tenant boundaries alone are insufficient and cache clearing is not an authorization mechanism.
    accepted change: Give principals independent business/matter grants and explicit active context. Key caches by tenant, principal/grant revision and audience; recheck on reads. Cross-business disclosure is a separately authorized action, including for a common owner.
    acceptance or revisit test: Switch businesses, revoke one grant and reuse a stale context/cache key; no other business evidence is disclosed. Add automated agent exchange only after a repeated authorized workflow justifies it.
MECHANISMS:
  [1]
    id: M01
    title: Coverage has a basis, not a green promise
    CONTRACTS:
      [1]
        C01

      [2]
        C03

      [3]
        C10

      [4]
        C16
    mechanism: A source window records the maximum provider scope, selected scope, observed interval, cursor/export/attestation basis, independent inventory provenance and unexplained delta. Processing counts reconcile the captured journal separately. A healthy session supports “observed since”, not proof of every message. Unknown denominators remain unknown.
    example: A corrected notice missing before the connector cannot be found by comparing the model to its own journal. A separate permitted inventory may detect the omission; if none exists, the report cannot claim end-to-end recall.
    test: FT01 / FT02
    boundary: Counts deduplicate by source identity/revision. Do not count multiple candidate records as multiple ingested messages.

  [2]
    id: M02
    title: Field authority survives external edits
    CONTRACTS:
      [1]
        C04

      [2]
        C11

      [3]
        C17
    mechanism: An authority binding identifies the external system/ref scheme, read method, observed revision/hash, freshness policy and write mode. A candidate/check binds that revision. A newer authoritative value stales the check; admission/writeback revalidates or stops for reconciliation. Cutover is explicit and former-authority edits are exceptions. Label an attested comparison with the named source and time; never imply it is a live authoritative-system read.
    example: The accountant changes a received quantity while an invoice discrepancy awaits approval. The old proposal is stale; accepting it must not overwrite the newer record.
    test: FT03
    boundary: No change feed or revision token means weaker observation. Use disclosed hash/manual reconciliation and avoid an unearned concurrency guarantee.

  [3]
    id: M03
    title: Cancellation is a protocol, not an undo button
    CONTRACTS:
      [1]
        C05

      [2]
        C06

      [3]
        C08
    mechanism: A transaction claims an authorized intent against current policy/grant/cancel epochs. A committed scope stop prevents later claims. Every before-send path persists transmit_started_at under current epochs before calling the provider. That marker conservatively means transmission may have occurred, not that it did. A prior stop can prevent the marker; a post-marker missing receipt remains unknown. Verify provider cancellation/completion; separately authorize compensation.
    example: An order is claimed, then the owner presses Stop. If no request was sent it may be prevented; if the supplier committed it, GoFathom cannot truthfully label it cancelled without a confirmed cancellation.
    test: FT04 / FT05
    boundary: Earlier claims can be in flight. Database atomicity does not extend across an uncontrolled provider. No blind resend after timeout.

  [4]
    id: M04
    title: Instructions need explicit override authority
    CONTRACTS:
      [1]
        C05

      [2]
        C12

      [3]
        C15
    mechanism: Store target/effect, scope selector, condition, issuer capability, stated/recorded/confirmed/effective times, timezone, expiry boundary, release condition, conflict set and explicit supersedes/override policy. Neither a newer timestamp nor a narrower instruction automatically defeats a hold. Ambiguity is held for a precise clarification. Instructions skipping confirmation must match an explicit tenant policy entry; show known affected work and due dates before consequential activation.
    example: A staff member says “credit note received, pay” while the owner’s supplier hold is active. Evidence of a credit is not authority to release the hold.
    test: FT06
    boundary: Low-risk explicit authenticated instructions may use pre-agreed confirmation rules. Consequential or ambiguous changes require exact review; models cannot choose a weaker change class to bypass controls.

  [5]
    id: M05
    title: Review capacity is visible operational state
    CONTRACTS:
      [1]
        C03

      [2]
        C07

      [3]
        C16
    mechanism: The queue shows risk, age, owner, SLA, pending volume and estimated effort. A review budget forecasts capacity; overflow triggers a backup reviewer/escalation and a visible backlog, not automatic acceptance or concealment. Batch only equivalent bounded proposals and bind every confirmation to its targets.
    example: Ramya has 20 notices awaiting review. The brief reports pending/unreviewed items and coverage even when the planned daily review budget is exhausted.
    test: FT07
    boundary: Opening evidence is not proof of thoughtful review. Use disclosed simulation exercises, spot checks and correction/outcome quality; diagnostic telemetry is not employee scoring.

  [6]
    id: M06
    title: A bounded runner with an accountable owner
    CONTRACTS:
      [1]
        C06

      [2]
        C08
    mechanism: Before live operation, name a runner owner and register job states, legal transitions, timer types, lease/fencing behavior, retry classes, outbox, cancel and version policy. Pin in-flight jobs to a supported definition; unknown versions are held. New orchestration primitives require a comparative engine review rather than unreviewed expansion.
    example: A proposed child workflow plus cross-job signal graph exceeds the initial charter. Compare an established engine under the same failure suite before extending the runner.
    test: FT08
    boundary: Domain reconciliation is mandatory and may run as a bounded job; it is distinct from building a generic compensation framework. Ownership is a required pilot field, not a currently assigned person.

  [7]
    id: M07
    title: Trust boundaries differ by worker
    CONTRACTS:
      [1]
        C02

      [2]
        C03

      [3]
        C05

      [4]
        C06
    mechanism: Define parser, inference, intake and effect capability profiles. A parser receives one scoped asset and a validated output channel; no production DB credentials, sensitive environment secrets or unrestricted network. Apply resource/time limits. Intake and effect workers have different narrowly scoped capabilities and auditable purposes.
    example: A PDF tries to fetch a URL or read a secret file. Its parser has neither the authority nor the credentials; legitimate derivative output still succeeds.
    test: FT09
    boundary: Isolation has to be demonstrated for the actual runtime. Merely using a container or calling a worker isolated proves nothing.

  [8]
    id: M08
    title: Discovery has frozen terms and honest evidence
    CONTRACTS:
      [1]
        C09

      [2]
        C13

      [3]
        C16

      [4]
        C18
    mechanism: Version and digest the pilot’s source window, eligible-event definition, comparison arms, risk slices, modalities, review burden, thresholds, price experiment and stop conditions before scoring. Amendments retain history and require a fresh comparable window. Observe baseline time where feasible and label self-report limitations. Record each authorized reliance decision in C18 with evidence versions, residual risks, review date and fallback.
    example: A late rule change would improve apparent recall by excluding hard notices. Keep the original score and run a separately versioned comparison instead of moving the denominator.
    test: FT10
    boundary: A paid commitment is stronger than a friendly verbal yes but is neither a prerequisite for bounded discovery nor proof of product-market fit. Unknown prices remain unknown.
TEST REGISTRY:
  [1]
    id: FT01
    title: Captured-event conservation
    CONTRACTS:
      [1]
        C01

      [2]
        C03

      [3]
        C10
    gate: G1
    stimulus: Replay one source revision twice; leave another pending; quarantine one; exclude one with a rule; let one message create three candidates and a burst support one candidate.
    expected: Captured source revisions reconcile once across pending/excluded/quarantined/failed/assessed states. Candidate links are many-to-many; no excluded event disappears from audit.
    execution status: Not executed: declarative test specification
    code ref: None
    run evidence: None

  [2]
    id: FT02
    title: Independent denominator and canary limits
    CONTRACTS:
      [1]
        C10

      [2]
        C13

      [3]
        C16
    gate: G1
    stimulus: Remove an eligible event before journal capture and another at routing; compare a separately sourced inventory. Include shared-failure and unknown-inventory variants.
    expected: Report observed omission or unknown denominator. Labeled real-event recall and known canary detection are separate; processing reconciliation alone never proves source completeness.
    execution status: Not executed: declarative test specification
    code ref: None
    run evidence: None

  [3]
    id: FT03
    title: Authority revision conflict
    CONTRACTS:
      [1]
        C04

      [2]
        C11

      [3]
        C17
    gate: G2
    stimulus: Change an external field after a check is proposed and before admission/writeback; edit the former authority after cutover.
    expected: Stale bound check cannot authorize overwriting the new value. Re-read/review or reconcile; dual-authority edits raise a visible exception.
    execution status: Not executed: declarative test specification
    code ref: None
    run evidence: None

  [4]
    id: FT04
    title: Revoke and cancel at each boundary
    CONTRACTS:
      [1]
        C05

      [2]
        C06

      [3]
        C08
    gate: G3
    stimulus: Revoke before claim, after claim/before send, during send, after remote commit and after lost receipt; race two dispatchers.
    expected: No claim after committed scope stop. Earlier claims receive truthful prevented/requested/verified-cancelled/completed/unknown labels. At most one valid local claim per intent generation; provider effects reconciled.
    execution status: Not executed: declarative test specification
    code ref: None
    run evidence: None

  [5]
    id: FT05
    title: Unknown effect and compensation
    CONTRACTS:
      [1]
        C06

      [2]
        C11
    gate: G3
    stimulus: Provider commits then times out; a retry arrives; later compensation is requested.
    expected: No blind duplicate action; reconcile first. Compensation requires its own current authorization and receipt. Unknown is never silently relabeled failed or cancelled.
    execution status: Not executed: declarative test specification
    code ref: None
    run evidence: None

  [6]
    id: FT06
    title: Instruction semantics and override
    CONTRACTS:
      [1]
        C05

      [2]
        C12

      [3]
        C15
    gate: G2
    stimulus: Apply a supplier hold; propose narrower subordinate release; use “until Friday” without boundary; supersede after dispatch claim.
    expected: Unauthorized release and ambiguous boundary are held. Explicit authorized overrides trace their target; prospective rules do not undo an already emitted effect. A model cannot invent a preauthorized instruction policy entry; affected-work preview names its coverage limits.
    execution status: Not executed: declarative test specification
    code ref: None
    run evidence: None

  [7]
    id: FT07
    title: Review backlog and exact confirmation
    CONTRACTS:

    stimulus: Exceed planned review capacity; submit two similar proposals; issue an ambiguous “OK”.
    expected: Backlog and age remain visible, escalation has an owner and nothing auto-accepts. Ambiguous confirmation binds to no proposal until clarified. Critical work is not hidden by budget caps.
    execution status: Not executed: declarative test specification
    code ref: None
    run evidence: None

    expected: Fence stale worker, preserve bounded timer/retry progress, hold unsupported definitions and trigger a runner/engine review. Reconcile effect uncertainty outside retry guessing.
    execution status: Not executed: declarative test specification

    expected: Permitted derivative still works; prohibited access is denied. Document actual prefilter exposure and measured persistence. Reject a deployment whose agreed privacy boundary cannot be met.
    execution status: Not executed: declarative test specification

RUNNER CHARTER:
  owner: Unassigned — must be named before live pilot
  SUPPORTED:
    [1]
      Registered job states and legal transitions

    [2]
      Leases with fencing generations

    [3]
      Declared bounded timer types per workflow

    [4]
      Classified bounded retry and dead-letter/review outcome

    [5]
      Transactional outbox and deduplicating consumers

    [6]
      Scoped cancellation and dispatch fencing

    [7]
      Pinned supported workflow definition per in-flight job
  REVIEW TRIGGERS:
    [1]
      Child orchestration or complex signal graphs

    [2]
      In-flight definition migration needs

    [3]
      Generic compensation framework

    [4]
      Recovery/cancellation incidents or growing operational toil
  review cadence: At phase exits and whenever a trigger occurs; no quarterly-only delay.
  boundary: Choose the simplest implementation that passes the same recovery/cancellation/version suite. Review does not automatically select Temporal. Domain effect reconciliation remains mandatory.
CHANGES:
  [1]
    disposition: Preserve
    title: Same 12 stations; Foundation 1.0 intact
    reason: The factory structure and platform vision remain. The new edition refines mechanisms and delivery gates; it does not turn every responsibility into pilot scope.

  [2]
    disposition: Repair
    title: Two different coverage checks
    reason: Independent inventory versus received events measures observed source coverage. Received revisions versus processing dispositions measures conservation. Unknown denominators and aged processing backlog stay visible.

  [3]
    disposition: Add
    title: C17: authority per field
    reason: Name authority, external identity/version, observation health, write mode and cutover. New external edits stale dependent proposals and checks.

  [4]
    disposition: Clarify
    title: Cancellation before and after transmission
    reason: A durable transmit marker is evidence of possible transmission, not proof of it. Serialize local fencing; reconcile outside effects and use evidence-backed UI labels.

  [5]
    disposition: Strengthen
    title: Instruction semantics and review capacity
    reason: Explicit override authority, scope, time boundaries and change classes; consequential holds are not automatically safe. Backlogs escalate rather than silently auto-accept.

  [6]
    disposition: Bound
    title: Runner and worker capabilities
    reason: An owned versioned runner charter limits custom infrastructure. Parser, intake and effect workers have distinct enforced capability profiles.

  [7]
    disposition: Separate
    title: Vendor cost, customer burden and combined cost
    reason: Customer time is not automatically a vendor cash expense. Model three views, count subscription as a transfer in combined economics, and label price assumptions.

  [8]
    disposition: Expose
    title: Debate, provenance and untested implementation
    reason: A twelve-decision log, declarative failure registry, code-audit template and source-path index show what changed, why and what has not been demonstrated.
DECISIONS:
  [1]
    id: GF-D01
    title: Begin with an evidence-led work board
    choice: Account for each source revision and workflow evaluation as pending, excluded with reason, quarantined, failed or assessed. Assessed events link to zero or more candidates; candidate matching and work status remain separate. Audit exclusions and replay changed rules.
    why: Owners and coordinators need a reliable next step, owner and supporting source, not another disconnected conversation.
    alternative: A universal personal assistant maximizes breadth; a narrow exception board makes missed work, review load and completion measurable.
    revisit when: A paid pilot demonstrates demand for adjacent workflows and enough shared semantics to add them.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC04

      [2]
        YC05

      [3]
        YC07

      [4]
        YC13
    proof: Reconcile a fixed journal window including pending/failed items. One message creates several candidates; several messages support one candidate; an excluded critical item is found by independent review.
    status: Proposed
    debate disposition: Amend
    delivery gate: Pilot / G1
    claude objection: Router-declined messages can disappear from every board lane.
    codex response: Accept complete intake accounting; reject one message → one candidate and terminal-only counts.

  [2]
    id: GF-D02
    title: Keep a single authority for each field
    choice: Bind each authoritative field to a system, source identity/version or hash, read method, observation window, write mode and cutover. Revalidate the bound revision before admission/writeback; external changes stale dependent checks.
    why: A second ungoverned stock or financial ledger creates disagreements that an agent cannot resolve by confidence.
    alternative: Marble suggests richer operational records; Definite suggests exact reconciliation. Take both patterns but explicitly name the owner of each quantity and status.
    revisit when: A customer authorizes a scoped migration with opening balance, cutover, reconciliation and rollback.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC08

      [2]
        YC18

      [3]
        YC14
    proof: Edit a source while review is pending; require re-review. After cutover, conflicting edits to the former authority raise a dual-write exception.
    status: Proposed
    debate disposition: Amend
    delivery gate: Pilot / G1–G2
    claude objection: The authority system is named in prose, but external edits can invalidate pending decisions.
    codex response: Accept C17; observation is bounded by actual connector capability, not a promised universal one-sync guarantee.

  [3]
    id: GF-D03
    title: Use a modular application with isolated workers
    choice: Untrusted parser gets only the scoped asset, no production secrets or direct database access, restricted filesystem/egress, resource limits and a validated derivative-output API. Trusted workers receive separate least-privilege profiles.
    why: A small team can trace a transaction and deploy coordinated contracts without paying for 12 service boundaries.
    alternative: One always-running VM per customer offers continuity but adds idle cost and secrets exposure. Independent services add operational overhead before load is measured.
    revisit when: Measured queue contention, isolation requirements or independent release cadence justify a split.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC02

      [2]
        YC13

      [3]
        YC14
    proof: Deny forbidden socket/filesystem/credential access; bound resource exhaustion; allow legitimate derivative submission and inspect quarantined failures.
    status: Proposed
    debate disposition: Retain with precise boundaries
    delivery gate: Before processing untrusted assets
    claude objection: An isolated parser may still hold broad database credentials and unrestricted egress.
    codex response: Accept worker profiles; differentiate untrusted parsers from trusted ingestion/effect services. Ordinary environment access is not itself a security failure.

  [4]
    id: GF-D04
    title: Keep the useful harness; make models replaceable
    choice: Audit every H/C responsibility with commit, code path or explicit absence, entrypoints, known divergent paths and test artifacts. Distinguish not audited, absent, partial, present-untested and tested-at-commit.
    why: The research does not prove the current harness should be rewritten or that every model behaves equivalently.
    alternative: Hermes supplies agent-loop patterns; an entire personal-agent product does not supply business grants or accepted records.
    revisit when: A measured quality, cost or maintainability gap remains after bounded fixes.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC01

      [2]
        YC12
    proof: Locate code and permitted fixtures; reproduce historical failures if available. A tested status requires pinned test evidence; the documentation template remains unfilled until then.
    status: Proposed
    debate disposition: Amend
    delivery gate: Discovery / G0
    claude objection: A module name can be mistaken for tested implementation; evidence labels are templated.
    codex response: Accept commit-pinned audit rows and divergent entrypoints. Historical par/CC-224 cases are reproduction targets, not asserted fail/pass results.

  [5]
    id: GF-D05
    title: Durable progression, conditional engine
    choice: Register job states, timer types and transitions. Support leases/fences, classified retries, outbox and scoped cancellation. Complex signal graphs, child orchestration or in-flight definition migration trigger a comparative engine spike. Domain effect reconciliation remains required.
    why: Work must survive crashes and waiting humans. SQL records remain authoritative whichever runner is chosen.
    alternative: Temporal handles durable workflow progression; Terse offers entity/command patterns. Neither automatically solves duplicate external effects or domain policy.
    revisit when: In-flight versioning, cancellation propagation, recovery complexity or operational toil exceeds the simpler runner.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC14

      [2]
        YC02
    proof: Test crash, stale lease, timer, cancellation and upgrade recovery. Review complexity at phase exit and on new primitives or incidents; compare engineering and operating effort.
    status: Proposed
    debate disposition: Amend
    delivery gate: Pilot / G1; review before runner expansion
    claude objection: A simple runner can grow into an unowned workflow engine.
    codex response: Accept a charter and owner; reject an arbitrary one-timer cap, quarterly-only review and automatic Temporal adoption.

  [6]
    id: GF-D06
    title: Minimum sufficient permissions
    choice: Disclose provider-visible scope and selected processing scope separately. Minimize nonselected content before durable capture, including controllable SDK cache/log/crash paths. Assess dedicated number/host, account risk and explicit exposure limits; reject incompatible deployments.
    why: Maximum awareness is not useful if confidential material reaches the wrong staff member or business.
    alternative: Screenpipe-style broader awareness can help later; it is not a prerequisite for WhatsApp/email workflows.
    revisit when: A measured blind spot cannot be solved by existing permitted sources and the owner chooses additional capture.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC03

      [2]
        YC10

      [3]
        YC16
    proof: Inject nonselected content in a controlled test and inspect journal, media, traces, cache and crash artifacts. State measured exclusions and unavoidable session exposure; do not promise zero traces without evidence.
    status: Proposed
    debate disposition: Amend
    delivery gate: Before any live source enrollment
    claude objection: Selected groups may be a filter rather than a restriction at the provider.
    codex response: Accept source-enforced versus application-filtered distinctions; inspect the actual adapter instead of assuming all sessions or Gmail labels have identical scopes.

  [7]
    id: GF-D07
    title: Build business semantics; reuse primitives selectively
    choice: Dependency records name provenance, rights, capabilities, provider/account constraints, failure owner and fallback mode with actual freshness limits. Only adopt what the chosen workflow needs.
    why: Public source is not proof of compatibility, license rights or production safety.
    alternative: Executor may reduce integration work; adopting it wholesale does not replace exact-action approvals and reconciliation.
    revisit when: Unresolved rights, security fixes or excessive maintenance cost require an alternative.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC01

      [2]
        YC16

      [3]
        YC18
    proof: Exercise selected connector recovery and a permitted import fallback; label manual/delayed operation and gaps rather than presenting it as live continuity.
    status: Proposed
    debate disposition: Retain with operational risk checks
    delivery gate: Pilot / chosen connectors
    claude objection: License checks miss protocol changes, provider terms and account restrictions.
    codex response: Accept an owner and fallback for external-service risks. Import success does not prove continuous capture.

  [8]
    id: GF-D08
    title: Deterministic authorization outside AI
    choice: Serialize local claims and durable before-send transmit markers with current grant/cancel epochs. A scope stop fences later boundaries. The marker means possible transmission, not success; earlier attempts may need reconciliation. Before-send prevention requires marker/fencing invariants on every path. Compensation is a new authorized action.
    why: A persuasive explanation or independent reviewer model cannot create authority.
    alternative: Decawork inspires contextual review; hard rules still decide absolute denies. Human approval cannot make false evidence true.
    revisit when: New action classes require new schemas, grants and tests, not broader system prompts.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC11

      [2]
        YC01

      [3]
        YC18
    proof: Inject revocation/cancel before claim, between claim/send, during send, after remote commit and after lost response. UI only claims prevented/cancelled/completed when evidence warrants it; otherwise unknown.
    status: Proposed
    debate disposition: Amend
    delivery gate: Before first external action / G3
    claude objection: Revocation, cancellation and a kill switch are underspecified once a request is in flight.
    codex response: Accept C06 policy/grant/epoch and cancellation evidence. Reject after claim = too late and atomic revocation across external systems.

  [9]
    id: GF-D09
    title: Progressively richer media
    choice: C16 records required input modalities, language/noise conditions and citation locator types. Use native structure when suitable; process required images/voice from the first selected slice.
    why: Most business value comes from preserving source evidence and asking the right small clarification, not processing every frame.
    alternative: Sidekick supports worker-friendly capture; Shire suggests continuous observation. Start with user-supplied evidence before ambient monitoring.
    revisit when: A measured workflow needs video temporal coverage or optional local capture and accepts its cost and consent boundary.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC07

      [2]
        YC03

      [3]
        YC15
    proof: Score real permitted media by risk slice, wrong extraction and abstention. Show page/region/time locators where applicable and unsupported coverage explicitly.
    status: Proposed
    debate disposition: Amend
    delivery gate: Workflow selection / G0
    claude objection: A blanket text-first launch could exclude evidence needed by the chosen photo/voice workflow.
    codex response: Accept required modalities per workflow; native-text-first is an extraction preference, not a product restriction. Video remains conditional on need.

  [10]
    id: GF-D10
    title: Govern change according to impact
    choice: Use policy-defined override capabilities, explicit target/supersedes links and scope checks. Hold incompatible unresolved rules. Define timezone/boundary/condition/release authority. Confirmation policy depends on target/risk; ambiguous or consequential changes require exact review.
    why: Fast operational control and trustworthy improvement have different lifecycles.
    alternative: Asakana inspires correction UX; GrepAI suggests tested procedures. Neither establishes that automatic self-training is appropriate.
    revisit when: Impact scope expands, a formerly benign alias affects financial/matter identity, or rollback proves insufficient.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC04

      [2]
        YC12
    proof: Cover owner hold versus subordinate release, ambiguous Friday, count-time thresholds, incompatible overlaps and action-in-flight supersession. Use replay/shadow plus protected future-case tests when risk requires.
    status: Proposed
    debate disposition: Amend
    delivery gate: Pilot / G2; controls before rule activation
    claude objection: Instruction conflict, override, expiry and change-class authority are not explicit.
    codex response: Accept semantic fields; reject rank-plus-specificity as a universal override rule and shadow activation as sufficient proof for every high-risk change.

  [11]
    id: GF-D11
    title: One portable evaluation contract
    choice: C10 separates source observation basis, known gaps and processing coverage. C16 identifies independent inventory/eligibility adjudication and denominator status. Report labeled real-event results, synthetic/canary results and unknown unseen coverage separately. Record risk-slice reliance in C18; combine appropriately limited evidence in an authorized assurance case rather than requiring or trusting one evidence type universally.
    why: Two overlapping evaluation platforms would fragment the definition of success.
    alternative: Hue helps manage episodes and comparison; Rystic helps simulate stateful dependencies. Neither owns the business oracle.
    revisit when: A purchased capability has proven fidelity, rights, data controls and lower total operating burden.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC06

      [2]
        YC17
    proof: Drop an event before intake and before routing; the comparison must detect or declare the unobservable gap. Live canaries require explicit consent and isolation from consequential workflows.
    status: Proposed
    debate disposition: Amend
    delivery gate: Pilot / G1 and every reliance expansion
    claude objection: Intake cannot be the sole source of its own eligible-event denominator.
    codex response: Accept independent inventories with provenance and known shared failure modes. Reject canaries as the only way to estimate rare-event recall or proof of natural-event recall.

  [12]
    id: GF-D12
    title: Defer cross-business agents and native capture
    choice: Give principals independent business/matter grants and explicit active context. Key caches by tenant, principal/grant revision and audience; recheck on reads. Cross-business disclosure is a separately authorized action, including for a common owner.
    why: Agent-to-agent transport does not prove business completion or authorize sharing.
    alternative: Agent Relay enables communication; the customer relationship, minimal evidence and verification protocol remain ours.
    revisit when: Two customers need a repeated shared workflow with demonstrated value and permitted data transfer.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC09

      [2]
        YC16
    proof: Switch businesses, revoke one grant and reuse a stale context/cache key; no other business evidence is disclosed. Add automated agent exchange only after a repeated authorized workflow justifies it.
    status: Proposed
    debate disposition: Retain with clarification
    delivery gate: Human roles when needed; automated delegation later
    claude objection: A CA or authorized operator may serve several businesses before agent exchange exists.
    codex response: Accept scoped human roles now; tenant boundaries alone are insufficient and cache clearing is not an authorization mechanism.
STAGES:
  [1]
    id: 01
    name: Join & establish trust
    phase: SET UP
    question: Who owns this workspace?
    purpose: Create a customer and business boundary before granting access. Signup is required for GoFathom; the saved reviews do not establish every vendor’s signup implementation.
    PARTS:
      [1]
        id: 01.1
        name: Account & sign-in
        deliverable: Maintained identity provider, sessions and recovery.
        mode: Reuse

      [2]
        id: 01.2
        name: Business workspace
        deliverable: Organization, outlets or chambers, and verified ownership.
        mode: Build

      [3]
        id: 01.3
        name: People & roles
        deliverable: Invitations, membership, manager/staff/CA roles and removal.
        mode: Build

      [4]
        id: 01.4
        name: Consent & boundaries
        deliverable: Explain selected access, purposes, retention and who sees what.
        mode: Build

      [5]
        id: 01.5
        name: Device enrollment
        deliverable: Register a phone/browser; bind optional desktop sessions to a principal.
        mode: Adapt
    inputs: Owner intent and verified identity.
    outputs: Workspace ID, memberships and initial access policy.
    gate: A user in Consu cannot read ForeFathers by switching an ID; removed members lose access.
    loop: Membership changes return here; account deletion has its own retention/export process.
    LAYERS:
      [1]
        L01

      [2]
        L02
    EXAMPLES:
      varun: Varun creates separate Consu and ForeFathers business scopes; staff and CA receive different roles.
      ramya: Arkaj creates the chamber workspace; Ramya can coordinate matters without unrestricted access for every staff member.
    COMPARISONS:
      [1]
        project: YC16
        approach: Inkbox contributes stable agent identity and conversation-bound authority; that is narrower than a complete business signup system.

      [2]
        project: YC01
        approach: Executor separates account connections from agent use; study that boundary after identity is established.

      [3]
        project: YC02
        approach: Agent37 contributes a recognizable personal agent workspace and continuity across devices; hosted tenancy is not audited.

      [4]
        project: YC10
        approach: Glen makes shared context ownership relevant; SupaBiz must own membership and source access rules.
    GOFATHOM:
      title: Identity before awareness
      mechanism: Create the owner account with a maintained identity provider; verify business ownership and invite roles. Keep business scopes separate even when an owner owns both. Staff need a capture/acknowledgment flow; managers get review and assignment; CA gets explicitly shared accounting material.
      ux: The signup screen explains what will be read, who can see it and how to disconnect. Do not ask for every permission on first launch.
      phase: Gate 0 → foundation
    historical sprint: S1
    baseline note: Original factory responsibility breakdown, carried forward with the GoFathom clarification above. Historical sprint IDs are not the new delivery plan.

  [2]
    id: 02
    name: Connect permitted sources
    phase: SET UP
    question: What may the system access?
    purpose: Connect only the accounts and groups needed for a workflow. Reading, sending, exporting and acting are separate capabilities.
    PARTS:
      [1]
        id: 02.1
        name: Connection broker
        deliverable: OAuth/session credentials stored outside model context.
        mode: Reuse

      [2]
        id: 02.2
        name: Source enrollment
        deliverable: Choose Gmail inboxes, WhatsApp groups and permitted app scopes.
        mode: Build

      [3]
        id: 02.3
        name: Capability map
        deliverable: Describe actual read/write/media/history limits per adapter.
        mode: Build

      [4]
        id: 02.4
        name: Connection health
        deliverable: Expiry, missing scopes, reconnect and coverage indicators.
        mode: Build

      [5]
        id: 02.5
        name: Revocation path
        deliverable: Disconnect credentials, stop jobs and invalidate affected context.
        mode: Build
    inputs: Workspace identity, user consent and provider credentials.
    outputs: Scoped connection IDs and a verified capability/coverage record.
    gate: Reconnect safely; never treat a quiet disconnected source as up-to-date. Existing WhatsApp group access remains an adapter validation task.
    loop: Expired access returns here; queued actions recheck permission before dispatch.
    LAYERS:
      [1]
        L02

      [2]
        L03
    EXAMPLES:
      varun: Enroll Consu’s operations group and a separate accountant group. Give the pilot read access before enabling reviewed sends.
      ramya: Connect Arkaj’s court inbox; scope which attachments and matter records staff may receive.
    COMPARISONS:
      [1]
        project: YC01
        approach: Executor centralizes integrations and credentials so multiple agents can use authorized connections.

      [2]
        project: YC16
        approach: Inkbox distinguishes quiet conversation intake, selective activation and the audience of each conversation.

      [3]
        project: YC03
        approach: screenpipe adds local screen/audio awareness, with capture controls; this is a later optional source, not a required connector.

      [4]
        project: YC02
        approach: Agent37 demonstrates environment continuity and browser handoff; that does not establish durable WhatsApp intake.

      [5]
        project: YC18
        approach: Definite’s read-oriented connection pattern is useful before allowing consequential writes.
    GOFATHOM:
      title: Every connector has a coverage contract
      mechanism: Distinguish maximum provider-visible scope from selected processing scope and record which boundary is provider-enforced versus application-filtered. Inspect the actual adapter, session/cache/log behavior and recovery owner. Minimize nonselected content before durable capture where controllable; disclose unavoidable exposure and reject incompatible deployments. Imports are delayed/manual fallbacks, not proof of live completeness.

        id: 12.1
        name: Correction capture
        deliverable: Preserve original evidence, old/new values and reason.
        mode: Build

      [2]
        id: 12.2
        name: Scoped proposal
        deliverable: Separate one-off fixes, operational instructions, tenant rules and reusable product changes by target and impact.
        mode: Build

      [3]
        id: 12.3
        name: Regression & held-out worlds
        deliverable: Versioned stateful cases, forbidden effects and protected answers.
        mode: Build

      [4]
        id: 12.4
        name: Release comparison
        deliverable: Quality, coverage, human effort, latency and full workflow cost.
        mode: Build

      [5]
        id: 12.5
        name: Versioned rollout
        deliverable: Review, activate, canary, observe and roll back a change.
        mode: Build
    inputs: Reviewed corrections, failures, incident traces and measured outcomes.
    outputs: Approved new workflow/context version or a rejected improvement proposal.
    gate: No customer’s correction becomes a global rule by default; a lower-cost change must preserve required outcome quality.
    loop: Reviewed changes return to stations 03/04; new events continue through station 05.
    LAYERS:
      [1]
        L10

      [2]
        L06

      [3]
        L05
    EXAMPLES:
      varun: A corrected supplier alias becomes a Consu-scoped mapping only after tests; it does not silently affect ForeFathers.
      ramya: A matter matching error becomes a regression case across courts and similar case numbers, not an unchecked memory note.
    COMPARISONS:
      [1]
        project: YC04
        approach: Asakana’s correction-driven UX is the priority inspiration; the underlying training mechanism is not established by demos.

      [2]
        project: YC06
        approach: Hue turns production incidents into repeatable cases and release comparisons.

      [3]
        project: YC17
        approach: Rystic contributes stateful simulated services, fault injection and outcome/forbidden-effect grading.

      [4]
        project: YC12
        approach: GrepAI contributes procedure optimization with draft/tested/active boundaries.

      [5]
        project: YC15
        approach: Shire inspires categorized reviewed observation corrections; evaluation must include coverage and false alerts.

      [6]
        project: YC18
        approach: Definite supports measured model substitution; no model is trusted solely by brand or fluency.
    GOFATHOM:
      title: Improve through explicit change classes
      mechanism: Classify changes by target and impact using trusted application rules; models can suggest, not lower controls. One-off fixes, explicit instructions, tenant rules and product changes have different release paths. Overrides need capability and explicit targets; harmful delays count as risk. Use replay, shadow and protected future cases as appropriate, with frozen prospective evaluation terms and separately labeled exploratory rescoring.
      ux: “Fix this item” differs from “Use this rule for this business.” Show effective time, examples, impact, reviewer and rollback history.
      phase: Every phase; releases after validation
    historical sprint: S0–S2, expanded S5
    baseline note: Original factory responsibility breakdown, carried forward with the GoFathom clarification above. Historical sprint IDs are not the new delivery plan.

        assessment_id

      [24]
        workflow_pack_version
    rule: Every captured source revision has an accountable processing disposition per workflow evaluation version: pending, excluded-with-reason, quarantined, failed or assessed. Assessed zero-candidate outcomes need reason codes and exclusion-equivalent audit/replay. Multiple candidates may share evidence and one event may create multiple candidates. Preserve revision history, dedupe and checkpoint atomicity. Processing assessments are a separate versioned relation keyed by source identity/revision, workflow pack and evaluation version; do not overwrite one shared source disposition across workflows.

Cancellation labels are prevented_before_send, requested, externally_cancelled_verified, completed_or_too_late_verified or unknown; compensation is a separately authorized action. No blind retry of a potentially committed effect.
