WORKFLOW CANDIDATES:
  [1]
    id: W-A
    name: Restaurant issue → verified closure
    buyer: Owner or operations manager
    trigger: Staff sends a photo/voice note about a leaking freezer.
    SEQUENCE:
      [1]
        Capture source IDs, outlet, media and coverage.

      [2]
        Locate the asset; ask a targeted question if uncertain.

      [3]
        Propose issue with observed evidence, not an invented diagnosis.

      [4]
        Manager accepts scope, assignee and expected completion proof.

      [5]
        Track acknowledgment, blockers and due time.

      [6]
        Manager reviews follow-up evidence and closes the issue; preserve recurrence history.
    authority: Existing operations process during shadowing; GoFathom tasks only after explicit cutover.
    why: Sidekick’s low-friction capture and herdr’s attention view may reduce forgotten work.
    test: Measure unreported/missed eligible issues, correct asset routing, review minutes, acknowledgment and closure time. No demand or percentage gain established.
    boundary: A photo cannot prove hidden electrical, hygiene or safety conditions.

  [2]
    id: W-B
    name: Receiving / invoice → reviewed exception
    buyer: Restaurant owner, purchasing lead or accountant
    trigger: Delivery note says 10 crates; receiving photo/voice suggests 8; invoice bills 10.
    SEQUENCE:
      [1]
        Link order, receiving evidence and invoice without merging their meanings.

      [2]
        Normalize item, unit and period using reviewed mappings.

      [3]
        Run exact quantity/value checks in code.

      [4]
        Show discrepancy or CANNOT_VERIFY with missing evidence.

      [5]
        Reviewer confirms accepted receipt and next follow-up.

      [6]
        Track supplier response/credit and reconcile with the authoritative accounting record.
    authority: Customer stock/accounting system; GoFathom owns exception and review history unless a ledger migration is separately agreed.
    why: Marble supplies domain separation; Asakana supplies focused corrections; Definite supplies exact checks.
    test: Measure discrepancy precision/recall, material missed amounts, reconciliation time and all reviewer/operator minutes.
    boundary: No automatic payment, duplicate inventory posting or assumption that invoice quantity equals received stock.

  [3]
    id: W-C
    name: Court email → reviewed matter work
    buyer: Principal and Ramya as operational user
    trigger: Court sends a notice, followed later by a correction.
    SEQUENCE:
      [1]
        Capture email, attachment, source revision and inbox coverage.

      [2]
        Match jurisdiction/court/matter identity; unresolved cases enter an ambiguous lane.

      [3]
        Extract cited date and type as a proposal; do not infer a statutory deadline.

      [4]
        Ramya verifies the notice and assigns the appropriate staff member.

      [5]
        Staff receives only matter-authorized evidence and acknowledges work.

      [6]
        Corrected notice reopens review and revises dependent reminders; completion needs the required document/filing evidence.
    authority: Existing legal process and reviewed source notices remain authoritative during shadowing.
    why: Praxis contributes matter-centered coordination; Glen suggests permission-aware context.
    test: Measure missed eligible notices, wrong matter matches, unsupported dates, acknowledgment and review time by risk class.
    boundary: No automatic legal conclusions, client disclosure or outsourced access to privileged material without explicit authorization.
CHANGE CLASSES:
  [1]
    name: One-off record correction
    example: This delivery had 8 crates, not 10.
    mechanism: Authorize editor; bind evidence and record revision; append correction; rerun dependent checks; show affected tasks. No standing rule is inferred.
    release: Record-level acceptance and audit; compensate downstream effects when needed.

  [2]
    name: Operational instruction
    example: Hold new orders from this supplier until Friday.
    mechanism: Verify issuer/scope; confirm effective time, expiry and affected action classes; activate C15; invalidate pending incompatible proposals. Forwarded messages are evidence, not authority.
    release: Operational confirmation, conflict resolution and expiry; no model training cycle.

  [3]
    name: Tenant dictionary or rule
    example: For this supplier, one crate of this SKU contains 12 units.
    mechanism: Preview historical and plausible future impacts; distinguish packaging/date versions; reviewer signs scoped rule. High-impact identity, quantity or financial rules need targeted regression/holdout tests.
    release: Versioned activation, limited rollout and rollback; tenant-only is not automatically low risk.

  [4]
    name: Reusable product / model change
    example: A revised parser handles mixed-language delivery notes.
    mechanism: Use consented/minimized examples; isolate tenant data; pin parser/prompt/model; run protected regression, fault and holdout suites. Training is optional, not assumed.
    release: Release report, canary, rollback and incident monitoring; never let the acting model promote itself.
BUILD STACK:
  [1]
    part: Customer application
    choice: React + TypeScript responsive web app if no suitable existing UI
    why: Phone capture/review and desktop coordination share one interface. Native wrappers wait for a proven OS need.
    gate: Proposed baseline; retain an adequate existing stack.

  [2]
    part: Control plane
    choice: TypeScript modular API; Fastify candidate
    why: Identity, business records, policy, work state and connectors have explicit modules and typed boundaries.
    gate: Audit current backend first; no framework rewrite for preference.

  [3]
    part: State & evidence
    choice: Managed PostgreSQL + object storage + secret manager
    why: Transactions/revisions/grants in SQL; original media and derivatives in object storage; credentials never in prompts.
    gate: Test actual non-owner runtime roles, backup/restore and current-grant file delivery.

  [4]
    part: Job execution
    choice: Persisted jobs / state machine; conditional Temporal spike
    why: Leases, retries, timers and cancellation survive worker restarts. Only one progression owner per job.
    gate: Compare complexity and recovery evidence; do not build a bespoke workflow engine indefinitely.

  [5]
    part: Model/media workers
    choice: Retain useful harness language; Python where parser ecosystem fits
    why: Isolate untrusted files, bound memory/CPU/network, version provider adapters and keep compute burstable.
    gate: Requalify fallbacks by data policy, modality and accuracy; LLM independence is not identical behavior.

  [6]
    part: Search/context
    choice: Exact IDs + SQL/full-text first; vector retrieval only for a measured gap
    why: Small, scoped context reduces irrelevant material and preserves accepted facts.
    gate: Current grants, provenance and revision-aware invalidation apply to every index.

  [7]
    part: Build environment
    choice: Monorepo, lockfiles, containerized dev, CI, separate test/staging/production
    why: Contract changes ship together; workers can still deploy separately. Domain code has no dependency on vendor SDK types.
    gate: Existing working environment preferred; Kubernetes/OpenHands are not product prerequisites.

  [8]
    part: Coding agents
    choice: Optional assistants in disposable development environments
    why: Useful for patches and tests with human code review; never the production authorization layer.
    gate: No customer credentials in development sandboxes; dependency/network scopes and output review remain explicit.
ROADMAP:
  [1]
    id: G0
    name: Access, baseline & product choice
    owner: Product lead + customer decision-maker + engineer
    deliver: Audit actual code and access. Observe current work; list eligible source events, gaps, reviewer time and consequences. Compare the three candidate workflows where data exists, select one and make a priced pilot offer. Produce the H/C code-audit table at a pinned commit and record reproduction outcomes (not yet attempted, reproduced, not reproducible, or blocked by rights/availability). Select required modalities and record buyer relationship/demand evidence.
    gate: Named buyer, reviewer, source authority and allowed exposure; usable consented sources; frozen versioned pilot terms and review/risk budget. Bounded discovery may precede a paid commitment. Resolve unavailable access before broad implementation.
    time: Two-week discovery/shadow timebox below; not a promise of a finished product.

  [2]
    id: G1
    name: Foundation & read-only shadow
    owner: Platform engineer + domain reviewer
    deliver: Identity/grants, one connector, durable intake, evidence storage, source coverage, candidate lanes and protected fixtures. Run beside the existing process. Add independent inventory provenance, complete processing accounting, C17 bindings, worker profiles and a named runner owner/charter.
    gate: Reconcile eligible-event denominator; no silent gaps; cross-tenant/revocation controls pass; compare omissions and reviewer minutes to manual work.
    time: Estimate after code/access audit. A shadow prototype does not certify reliance.

  [3]
    id: G2
    name: Reviewed work, one complete loop
    owner: Workflow engineer + customer operator
    deliver: Evidence drawer, accept/correct/hold, one domain schema, acknowledged assignments, closure proof and C15 instruction history. Cut over only explicitly scoped internal records. Add exact override/time semantics, review queue aging/backups and external-revision stale-check propagation.
    gate: Owner accepts field results and workload; disagreement/unknown items remain visible; changed evidence propagates; correction rollback works.
    time: Prioritize the smallest usable loop, not all 76 planning packages.

  [4]
    id: G3
    name: First authorized external action
    owner: Platform/security owner + workflow engineer
    deliver: Choose one action type. Implement exact approval, gateway, idempotency, effect ledger, readback, reconciliation and kill switch. Serialize claims/transmit markers with grant/cancel epochs; a scoped stop lists in-flight effects and uses truthful verified/unknown labels. Prefer an action with provider idempotency or reliable readback; include unresolved-outcome review cost in the choice.
    gate: Pass the declarative FT04/FT05 scenarios in a real implementation, including stale-worker/bypass paths. Enable only an expressly approved action/risk slice after a documented assurance review.
    time: No automatic purchasing, payment or legal deadline inference as a first action.

  [5]
    id: G4
    name: Reliability, economics & paid operation
    owner: Engineering lead + operations owner + buyer
    deliver: Restore rehearsal, incident response, support ownership, source recovery, cost attribution, constrained rollout and rollback. Confirm a paid service/product boundary.
    gate: Agreed risk/coverage/review targets hold over representative operation; total cost and support burden fit the offer; unresolved critical incidents block expansion.
    time: Duration follows event coverage and failure evidence, not an arbitrary calendar.

  [6]
    id: G5
    name: Expand from observed pull
    owner: Product + platform leads
    deliver: Add a second workflow or source only with evidence. Qualify optional desktop capture, advanced retrieval, video, delegated operators and agent-to-agent exchange separately.
    gate: Incremental value exceeds integration/review cost and regressions pass; new privacy and authority boundaries are designed before rollout.
    time: Native collaboration and WhatsApp replacement remain optional long-term directions.
FAILURE TESTS:
  [1]
    case: FT01 · Captured-event conservation
    stimulus: Replay one source revision twice; leave another pending; quarantine one; exclude one with a rule; let one message create three candidates and a burst support one candidate.
    expected: Captured source revisions reconcile once across pending/excluded/quarantined/failed/assessed states. Candidate links are many-to-many; no excluded event disappears from audit.

  [2]
    case: FT02 · Independent denominator and canary limits
    stimulus: Remove an eligible event before journal capture and another at routing; compare a separately sourced inventory. Include shared-failure and unknown-inventory variants.
    expected: Report observed omission or unknown denominator. Labeled real-event recall and known canary detection are separate; processing reconciliation alone never proves source completeness.

  [3]
    case: FT03 · Authority revision conflict
    stimulus: Change an external field after a check is proposed and before admission/writeback; edit the former authority after cutover.
    expected: Stale bound check cannot authorize overwriting the new value. Re-read/review or reconcile; dual-authority edits raise a visible exception.

  [4]
    case: FT04 · Revoke and cancel at each boundary
    stimulus: Revoke before claim, after claim/before send, during send, after remote commit and after lost receipt; race two dispatchers.
    expected: No claim after committed scope stop. Earlier claims receive truthful prevented/requested/verified-cancelled/completed/unknown labels. At most one valid local claim per intent generation; provider effects reconciled.

  [5]
    case: FT05 · Unknown effect and compensation
    stimulus: Provider commits then times out; a retry arrives; later compensation is requested.
    expected: No blind duplicate action; reconcile first. Compensation requires its own current authorization and receipt. Unknown is never silently relabeled failed or cancelled.

  [6]
    case: FT06 · Instruction semantics and override
    stimulus: Apply a supplier hold; propose narrower subordinate release; use “until Friday” without boundary; supersede after dispatch claim.
    expected: Unauthorized release and ambiguous boundary are held. Explicit authorized overrides trace their target; prospective rules do not undo an already emitted effect. A model cannot invent a preauthorized instruction policy entry; affected-work preview names its coverage limits.

  [7]
    case: FT07 · Review backlog and exact confirmation
    stimulus: Exceed planned review capacity; submit two similar proposals; issue an ambiguous “OK”.
    expected: Backlog and age remain visible, escalation has an owner and nothing auto-accepts. Ambiguous confirmation binds to no proposal until clarified. Critical work is not hidden by budget caps.

  [8]
    case: FT08 · Runner charter and upgrade
    stimulus: Crash after lease claim; run a stale worker; restart a timer; deploy an unknown job definition; request a new unsupported orchestration primitive.
    expected: Fence stale worker, preserve bounded timer/retry progress, hold unsupported definitions and trigger a runner/engine review. Reconcile effect uncertainty outside retry guessing.

  [9]
    case: FT09 · Parser boundary and source minimization
    stimulus: Attempt prohibited file/network access and resource exhaustion; inject nonselected chat content into a controlled adapter fixture; inspect storage/log/cache/crash paths.
    expected: Permitted derivative still works; prohibited access is denied. Document actual prefilter exposure and measured persistence. Reject a deployment whose agreed privacy boundary cannot be met.

  [10]
    case: FT10 · Frozen experiment and model qualification
    stimulus: Change eligibility after results, swap model/parser, use unavailable observer and expose oracle answers to acting model.
    expected: Original results remain; amended experiment has new digest/window. Model swap reruns qualified cases; unobservable episode is ungradable; oracle leakage invalidates evaluation. A changed or expired reliance decision prevents expansion of the allowed automation scope.

  [11]
    case: FT11 · Human multi-business isolation
    stimulus: A CA/operator switches businesses, reuses a cached result and then loses one grant; try sharing under a common owner.
    expected: Active context and current scoped grants govern reads/exports; cache key and invalidation cannot substitute for authorization. Cross-business disclosure needs an explicit allowed purpose.

  [12]
    case: FT12 · Required modalities and citations
    stimulus: Feed permitted blurred photo, noisy Hinglish audio, text-only email and sampled video as required by the chosen workflow.
    expected: Return supported cited candidates or visible uncertainty; modality coverage and wrong-extraction/abstention reported per risk slice; no unsupported hidden-condition inference.
QUESTIONS:
  [1]
    id: Q01
    question: Which first workflow has a buyer and usable source access?
    evidence needed: Customer observation + priced offer
    boundary: Do not expand into three verticals before a bounded pilot is chosen.

  [2]
    id: Q02
    question: Can the selected WhatsApp session reliably observe selected groups and media?
    evidence needed: Adapter coverage/reconnect experiment
    boundary: Record account owner, host, recovery owner and fallback; authentication alone is insufficient.

  [3]
    id: Q03
    question: What actual product code already works?
    evidence needed: Code audit + reproducible baseline
    boundary: Research pages and earlier reported harness results do not establish current implementation.

  [4]
    id: Q04
    question: Does a human-assisted exception desk improve adoption and economics?
    evidence needed: Authorized restaurant-side service trial
    boundary: Measure review quality, access boundaries, labor and margin; do not presume legal outsourcing is acceptable.

  [5]
    id: Q05
    question: When does a workflow engine beat the SQL runner?
    evidence needed: Same failure suite + operations cost
    boundary: Require evidence from versioning, cancellation, recovery and support toil.

  [6]
    id: Q06
    question: What reliability is enough for reliance?
    evidence needed: Risk-specific, pre-agreed pilot acceptance
    boundary: No universal percentage or small zero-failure sample proves safety; preserve manual fallback.

  [7]
    id: Q07
    question: Which models, region and suppliers meet the data/cost requirements?
    evidence needed: Provider qualification and procurement
    boundary: No current vendor quote, compliance certification or production region is assumed.

  [8]
    id: Q08
    question: What is the correct business identity and source of truth?
    evidence needed: Owner-confirmed entity and field authority map
    boundary: Do not merge Consu/Concu or replace customer records based on assistant guesses.
COST:
  status: Illustrative assumptions, not quotes or validated prices.
  currency: INR
  schema version: 1.1.0
  formula: vendor cash = fixed + model + media + storage + provider review + support; customer burden = subscription + customer review value; combined resources = vendor cash + customer review value (subscription excluded as transfer)
  DEFAULT:
    businesses: 5
    fixed: 10000
    events: 50000
    route fraction: 0.15
    model event cost: 0.6
    audio minutes: 2000
    audio rate: 0.4
    pages: 3000
    page rate: 0.25
    video minutes: 100
    video rate: 2
    storage gb: 100
    storage rate: 2
    provider review hours: 0
    provider labor rate: 300
    customer review hours: 40
    customer labor rate: 300
    support: 5000
    completed: 1000
    price per business: 10000
  NOTES:
    [1]
      All source volumes and review hours are totals across the businesses; price and business count calculate subscription revenue. Price is a placeholder for sensitivity analysis, not a G0 pricing anchor.

    [2]
      Provider/operator review belongs in vendor cash only when GoFathom pays it. Customer review is opportunity cost at an explicit valuation, not an automatic cash expense. Do not count the same reviewer twice.

    [3]
      Vendor contribution = subscription revenue minus modeled vendor cash; excludes taxes, sales, founder salaries, onboarding and omitted costs. It is not net profit.

    [4]
      Customer burden = subscription plus customer review opportunity cost; benefit has not been measured. Combined resource cost excludes subscription because it is a transfer between the parties.

    [5]
      Cost per verified completion uses genuinely completed outcomes; zero completions is undefined. Simulated/default values never establish real margins or improvement.
COMPLEXITY:
  [1]
    path: Entity lookup
    baseline: O(N) scan; naive all-pairs matching O(N²)
    approach: Indexed exact lookup O(log N + k), then bounded candidate checks
    space: O(N) index plus record storage
    limit: Fuzzy matching can still approach all-pairs behavior; cap candidates and measure ambiguity.

  [2]
    path: Source dedupe / journal
    baseline: Repeated work on every redelivery; no bounded completion guarantee
    approach: B-tree identity lookup/insert O(log E); O(E) total retained events
    space: O(E + media bytes)
    limit: Database contention, revisions and retention alter real throughput; stable provider identity is required.

  [3]
    path: Context assembly
    baseline: Send all retained history, O(T) tokens per request
    approach: Retrieve k relevant items, bound assembled tokens B; permission checks on all selected items
    space: O(N) search index plus bounded per-run context
    limit: No constant-time retrieval guarantee; loss of recall must be measured. LLM attention cost depends on model implementation.

  [4]
    path: Image / video processing
    baseline: Process all F frames or whole assets at full resolution
    approach: Process selected f frames or relevant regions, f ≤ F
    space: O(retained assets + derivatives)
    limit: Work often scales with processed bytes/frames but sampling may miss events; no accuracy equivalence assumed.

  [5]
    path: Work board / timers
    baseline: Repeated full scan of all tasks N
    approach: Index by tenant/status/due time: O(log N + k) for page or due batch
    space: O(N) task/timer state
    limit: Worst-case many due tasks still require O(N) work; fair scheduling and concurrency limits matter.

  [6]
    path: Version-guarded transition
    baseline: Long AI computation while holding locks
    approach: AI outside transaction; short conditional update and transactional outbox
    space: O(history + pending work)
    limit: Retries under contention and remote latency remain; no global exactly-once claim.
CRITIQUE:
  instructions: Critique Foundation 1.1 against its preserved 1.0 predecessor and the adjudication ledger. Decisions and declarative tests remain proposals. Do not treat agreement between Codex and Claude as empirical validation.
  PROTOCOL:
    [1]
      Read llms-full.txt and blueprint.json; use stable GF-D, stage, layer, H and C IDs.

    [2]
      For each objection cite the exact decision, assumption and source or mark it as a hypothesis.

    [3]
      Give the strongest alternative, user benefit, new failure modes and maintenance/operational cost.

    [4]
      Specify a falsifiable test and the observation that would change the decision.

    [5]
      Distinguish blocker, pilot experiment, later optimization and unsupported preference.

    [6]
      Preserve hard grants, protected oracles and equivalent safeguards in every comparison arm.

    [7]
      Do not invent performance percentages, customer demand, completed integrations or legal conclusions.

    [8]
      Return a proposed change set with accepted/rejected/deferred recommendations and unresolved disagreements.

    [9]
      Check whether accepted refinements are propagated across stages, layers, contracts and tests.

    [10]
      Keep source gaps, processing gaps, candidate matching, admission and effect outcome as separate dimensions.

    [11]
      Read debate.json for qualified/rejected recommendations; challenge remaining assumptions with falsifiable evidence.

    note: Durable workflow execution; engine selection remains an experiment; reviewed 18 October 2026.

    url: https://docs.temporal.io/activity-execution
    note: Cancellation is cooperative; an outside effect still needs evidence/reconciliation. Reviewed 18 October 2026.

    id: ENG-ISOLATION
    url: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/transaction-iso.html
    note: Local transaction concurrency/isolation must support the selected invariants; this does not make provider effects atomic. Reviewed 18 October 2026.
